MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  March 28, 2023
A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Goodell at 5:00 p.m., on March 28, 2023, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on March 23, 2023, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. A copy was also posted
at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive and Norman P. Murray
Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Bucknum
  Council Member Ruesch
  Council Member Vasquez
  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley
  Mayor Goodell

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk
  Renata Winter, Assistant City Clerk

CS1. Labor Negotiations - The Council Will Provide Direction to its Labor Negotiator

  Negotiations Are the City and City’s Unrepresented Employees. The City’s Negotiator
  is Dennis Wilberg.

CS2. Conference with Labor Negotiators Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957.6(a):
  Agency Negotiators: City Manager Dennis Wilberg; Assistant City Manager Keith

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:01 pm, Mayor Goodell recessed to Closed Session. The City Council reconvened
at 6:02 pm with all City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that on both matters the City Council was updated and gave
direction to their labor negotiators but no reportable action occurred.

INVOCATION: Tarik Ata from the Orange County Islamic Foundation

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Ruesch

PRESENTATIONS

P1. Presentation by O.C. Human Relations

  Received presentation from Charla Batey of the OC Human Relations Council.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

James Farris, M.V.: Voiced concerns with woke-like political direction city staff has gone to. He
outlined many problems all over the City and criticized the criminal justice system.

Michelle O’Brien, M.V. Announced that the Elks Lodge will have a booth at the upcoming City’s
Earth Day Event.

Ethan Diaz, Coto de Caza; Delanye Giraudi, Rancho Santa Margarita; Sophie Pennell, San
Clemente: Spoke on the relevance of a community theater in the City.

Margaret Thilken, M.V.; Tyler Van Der Aart, Ladera Ranch; Octaviano Roges IV, Coto de Caza:
Spoke in support of a community theater in the City.

Joshua Vecchione, M.V.: Commented on the students that spoke prior to him and how delighted
he is with them for speaking about their love for theater. He explained how important theater was
to him growing up and gave his background in the theater community. He hopes the City Council
will consider a theater for the residents.

Irene Vecchione, M.V.: Outlined the many benefits of a community theater in the City. She
spoke about the heart of our City and the passion a theater will bring to the community.

City Council Minutes  2  March 28, 2023
 Connie Lanzisera, M.V.: Addressed concerns on the agreement with Venture Strategic specifically
that all cities on the task force should share in the cost and asked for a quantifiable approach to the
cost for this agreement along with a more detailed description of the work to be done. . Asked that
this item be pulled from the Consent Calendar.

Carlos Pianelli, M.V: Spoke on the Value Rock’s potential project and voiced his concerns.

Michael Schlesinger, M.V.: Asked why the City has not completed its 6th Cycle Housing Element
Plan and asked that the City make this a top priority. He voiced concerns that developers will be
able to build new developments without Mission Viejo’s approval.

Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: Voiced her opposition to the agreement with Venture Strategic. Stated that
it was not a bid contract and the firm is politically connected and she questioned its ethics. She
recapped her report when she was on the City Council and quoted Congressman Darrell Issa
regarding Sober Living Homes. She closed her comments with a heartfelt thank you to Nashville
Police Department for their heroic actions yesterday and asked that City Hall be lit with blue lights
in support of our police officers.

Robert Breton, M.V: Spoke in support of a community theater and outlined his experience in
performing throughout the world and what impact this had on him growing up.

Items 14 and 19 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate consideration.

Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

  Council Member Bucknum presented a report.

Council Member Bucknum asked for a Point of Order to address some of the questions that were
asked under Public Comments.

Director of Community Development Elaine Lister noted that the City does have an adopted
Housing Element and we have rezoned our housing sites by the statutory deadline in 2021. The
Housing Element has been our priority. We have submitted to the State twice and received
numerous pages of comments. There are numerous new laws to be addressed. She stated that the
prior Housing Element Consultant was not making progress with the new laws and requirements.
We have a new consultant on board that his making progress and the document is currently being
formatted and we hope to have it to the Commission May or June of this year and then to the
Council thereafter. She answered Mayor Goodell’s question that approximately 19 out of 34 cities
in Orange County have not been certified by the State. Council Member Vasquez asked if item
#12 was an accurate report of the Housing Element. Director Lister responded that is correct.

NEW BUSINESS

20. Mid-Year Budget Review for FY 2022-2023

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas presented the staff report.

  Robert Breton, M.V.: Spoke on the 2015 Cultural Arts Master Plan that the Council adopted
  in March of 2015. He asked that the City Council adopt a budget appropriation amendment
  to pay for the hiring of a qualified consultant in the field of arts facility planning to assess
  the feasibility, analyze the market, study of costs, funding sources, revenue projections, and
  location. He suggested the location fields one and two right next to the Orchard Terrace at
  the Community Center.

City Council Minutes  6  March 28, 2023
   Michael Schlesinger, M.V.: He commented that the mid-year budget report lacked clarity in
  item 15 regarding the $410,000 increase of legal fees, as well as the $269,000 for the aquatics
  center and asked for more information. Voiced concerns on the Nadadores expenditures.

  Motion made by Council Member Ruesch, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, to add
  $100,000 for a consultant to assess a proposal for a performing arts center and to look for
  methods to find funding.

  Council Member Vasquez asked if there could be more detail on the $410k for legal fees.

  City Attorney Curley responded that it does not affect standard normal operating, it is dealing
  with unique circumstances that the City is finding itself dealing with. He stated all City legal
  affairs are privileged.

  Mayor Kelley asked for more full shade structures for upcoming park renovations.

  Council Member Vasquez questioned the natural gas usage at the aquatics center and asked
  if we can revisit some of the expenses and cost-sharing with the Nadadores.

  Mayor Goodell asked if we should put money aside of approximately $300,000 for the Vision
  Plan for the Oso Creek Golf Course. He asked if Council Member Ruesch would amend his
  motion.

  Council Member Ruesch amended the motion as follows:

  Motion made by Council Member Ruesch, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, to (1) adopt
  Resolution 23-10 Amending the FY 2022-23 Budget for Adjustments to Certain Revenue
  Sources and Operating and Capital Improvement Program Appropriations, with the addition
  of $100,000 for a consultant to assess a proposal for a performing arts center in the City and
  $300,000 for the continuation of the Golf Course and Open Space Vision Plan; and (2) adopt
  Resolution 23-11 Amending the City's Salary Schedule to be Effective April 1, 2023

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

27. City of Mission Viejo Participation in and Lead Role in Managing the Cities
  Collaborative Amicus Brief Participation in the City of Costa Mesa’s Petition to the
  U.S. Supreme Court

  City Attorney Bill Curley presented the report.

  Linn Hillman, M.V.: Asked what the City’s position is on the Amicus Brief. She feels we
  have an obligation to those that have less ability to live their lives well to take care of them.
  It is her belief that the State is pushing this so that City’s take responsibility for those less
  fortunate.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to
  authorize participation in and management of the amicus brief, from cities, in support of the
  petition of the City of Costa Mesa.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

28. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended ~ AB1234

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars
  as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

Council Member Bucknum

Council Member Bucknum encouraged residents to attend the many events at the Paseo on the
third Saturday of each month. She spoke to the Board of Directors of the South Orange Country
Economic Coalition at Providence Mission Hospital. She spoke on the tragedy in Nashville and
announced there is a national pray vigil tomorrow night at 7:00 pm. Council Member Bucknum
thanked law enforcement for keeping our community safe by working with our schools and
churches.

Council Member Ruesch

Council Member Ruesch outlined his events attended: Chamber Quad Mixer, Chamber
Daybreakers, US Army Ribbon Cutting, School of Rock, Dr. Mammone Memorial, the Olympic
Presentation by Mayor Goodell, and the Orange County Fire Authority large animal
demonstration. He suggested that when the Investment Advisory Commission meets that they

City Council Minutes  11  March 28, 2023
 review the banks that our investments are in and give us input on possibilities of how our
investments as far as returns may or may not change and that they report back the City Council.

Council Member Vasquez

Council Member Vasquez said she has been busy with meetings and ride-a-longs. She announced
that her younger daughter Helena just turned 7 and came in fourth place at her end of session
Strategic Kids Chess Tournament. She spoke about going to Los Angeles with her husband’s
family to sign a sacred book containing over 125,000 Japanese Americans that were incarcerated
in the camps during World War II which included her father-in-law, her husband’s grandfather
and aunt and her mother-in-law’s best friend that recently passed away. She talked about a very
famous photograph that a family friend and her father-in-law were in. Council Member Vasquez
explained that her Sister-in-law won an Emmy in 2022 for a mini documentary called Three Boys
Manzanar. She said it was a very moving experience and the goal of this book is to remember all
of the people that were interned during this time and not to forget this very important time in our
history. The book contains special ceramic pieces made from the soil collected from each of the
seventy-five incarceration sights and it is available for anyone to stamp. She went on a ride-a-long
with Deputy Cole. Lastly, she mentioned that her daughter Helena attended a Girl Scout
International Fair where different troops represent a different country with food from that country.
The Daisy Troop her daughter is in got to purchase the different foods.

Mayor Pro Tem Kelley

Mayor Pro Tem Kelley suggested that the City create a page on the City’s website that would keep
the residents informed about the Garden Plaza. She said she has received many questions on this
and would find that this to be helpful in transparency so the public has the ability to be informed.
Mayor Pro Tem Kelley also asked if staff could report at the next meeting on AB 2011 and SB 6.
She highlighted events attended: The Memorial for Dr. Michael Mammone, and the Ribbon
Cutting for the U.S. Army Center. She announced that Mission Viejo has been recognized as 8th
Safest City in California.

Mayor Goodell

Mayor Goodell thanked his colleagues for covering the many events throughout the City. He
mentioned that this past Sunday there was a really nice turnout for the Mayor’s presentation
“Mission Viejo and the Olympics: Past, Present and Future”. He stated that it was recorded and
encouraged residents to watch on the City’s website.
